The 2026-08-30 pass is a real UI change, not a re-render: the rail took VS Code's macOS activity-bar geometry (48px rail and 48px items against the previous 52/44, a 2px full-height active marker against 3px) and its glyphs dropped from 24px to 20px. The pages band was then replaced outright by a horizontal separator above the pages group: the band did not read at the native rail's density (measured 8/255 off the rail as a fill, 15 with rules) and the rule lands at 129 against a 30 rail. The web client keeps the band — see docs/client/ux/shell.md §2.1. The rail is 49px from 2026-08-30, not 48: it gained its own 1px right edge, without which it and the Explorer beside it were the same colour and ran together. Items are 48 wide but 40 tall from the same pass, following VS Code's glyph-to-item ratio rather than its pixel count, since our 20px SVG glyph puts more ink on screen than its 24px codicon. The glyphs were re-centred too — the active marker's left border had been reserved on one side only, putting every glyph 1px off axis. Rewritten 2026-08-01 onto the ROLE model: it lists the Roles the account holds and derives the permission breakdown from them through the same default role->permission map the server enforces with, replacing the coarse Administrator/Operator/Observer pill that read the retired AccessRights bitmask - a pill that would have kept asserting authority for an account whose Role had been revoked. The generator wires the real attribute service straight into the client, so the client's empty ServiceContext -- which a real server would have replaced with the session's identity -- reads as ANONYMOUS and the attribute is refused, collapsing the whole panel to 'No data'. Populating this capture found a teardown crash: ~SheetCell erases itself from SheetModel::blinking_cells_, which was declared after `cells_` and so destroyed before them — closing a sheet holding one blinking cell segfaulted in std::set::erase, reachable by any user whose custom table binds a cell to a live value. The activity rail's third zone: the utilities pinned at its foot behind an expanding spacer — Settings, and Users for an admin session. The marker sits on Users because a utility's marker means 'that view is what the workspace is showing' rather than 'this was clicked'. The pages group's '+' is hidden for this capture; it is added unconditionally by the rail's constructor and would otherwise lead a picture of the zone next door.
